q: A pipeline table has `CONSTRAINT valid_temp EXPECT (temperature BETWEEN -50 AND 60)` with no `ON VIOLATION` clause. What happens to a row with `temperature = 999`?
o: It is dropped
It is written to the table and counted as a violation
The update fails
It is moved to a quarantine table automatically
e: Without an `ON VIOLATION` clause an expectation only warns: the row is kept and the violation is recorded in the metrics.

q: One row in an update violates an expectation declared with `ON VIOLATION FAIL UPDATE`. What is written to the target table in that update?
o: Every row except the bad one
Only the rows processed before the bad one
Nothing: the update fails for that table
All rows, with a flag column on the bad one
e: `FAIL UPDATE` stops the update and nothing is committed for that flow. Someone has to fix the data or the rule and run it again.

q: The business wants bad readings removed from silver but kept somewhere for review. Which design fits?
o: `expect_or_fail` on the silver table
A warn expectation on silver
A `CHECK` constraint on silver
`expect_or_drop` on silver plus a second table that selects rows matching `NOT (rule)`
e: That is the quarantine pattern: the clean table drops the bad rows, and a second table with the inverse rule keeps them for inspection.

q: A Delta table has `CHECK (amount > 0)`. A job inserts 1,000 rows and 3 of them have `amount = 0`. What is the result?
o: The whole INSERT fails and no rows are committed
997 rows are committed and 3 are dropped
All 1,000 rows are committed and a warning is logged
The 3 rows are written with `amount` set to NULL
e: Delta constraints are checked on every write. A violation fails the whole transaction; there is no row-level drop.

q: Why should a quarantine rule be written as `temperature IS NOT NULL AND temperature BETWEEN -50 AND 60` instead of only the `BETWEEN` part?
o: `BETWEEN` does not work on DOUBLE columns
For a NULL temperature both the rule and `NOT (rule)` are NULL, so the row would land in neither table
Expectations require an `IS NOT NULL` in every rule
It makes the rule run faster
e: SQL uses three-valued logic. `NOT (NULL)` is still NULL, so a filter keeps the row in neither the clean nor the quarantine table. An explicit NULL test makes the rule always true or false.
